Magical gene / spots and rings

Angler

Strings of faintly glowing lights strung horizontally along the body, each light a pale core inside a deeper rim, like the lures of a deep-water fish.

What it does

AnglerRound and oval lights in strings that run horizontally along the body and bend as they go, never singly - a string is two lights at least. Each light is a pale core inside a deeper rim of the same hue, and one horse carries one design throughout. The strings turn vertical on the face and legs, where nothing else on this horse runs level. Mane, tail and hooves are untouched however close a string passes.
Angler carrierOne copy shows nothing. Two carriers bred together are the only way the lights appear.
Wild typeNo lights.

What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 5,000 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/angler.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.angler
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority302 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order
AllelesAng · n
Varies per horse5 values drawn once off the expressing allele copy, so a foal that inherits the copy inherits the look
Built fromAXIS, SPOTS, STROKES, TOWARD, emissive

What it paints

Angler

  1. the rim of each light, strung along the body — SPOTS × STROKES, painted with TOWARD, and it glows
  2. the pale core inside each light — SPOTS × STROKES, painted with TOWARD, and it glows
  3. strings running vertically down the face — SPOTS × STROKES, painted with TOWARD, and it glows
  4. strings running vertically down the legs, clear of the hoof — SPOTS × STROKES × AXIS, painted with TOWARD, and it glows
